quarterly_data.quarter: Oklo press release: Oklo to Advance Groves-2 Forge as Part of U.S. Department (10-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Oklo will advance Groves-2 Forge, an isotope production and processing pilot facility building on its Groves Isotope Test Reactor in Texas, as part of the DOE National Reactor Innovation Center's Nuclear Energy Launch Pad initiative (12 developers selected on 13 new projects). Groves-2 Forge is planned to integrate reactor irradiation with hot-cell processing (isotope separation, product recovery, packaging and transportation), will initially focus on producing lutetium-177 and other therapeutic isotopes for radiopharmaceutical treatments, and Oklo plans to transition it from pilot operations to commercial-scale isotope production with the appropriate NRC licenses for commercial operation. The release states Oklo brought the Groves Isotope Test Reactor from greenfield to criticality in less than a year, which it calls the first Reactor Pilot Program project to do so on private land (company claim). CEO Jacob DeWitte: 'Groves-2 Forge will build directly on that foundation by adding the capabilities needed to irradiate target materials and process and prepare valuable isotopes.'
quarterly_data.figure: selected among 12 developers on 13 projects; initial focus lutetium-177
